evidence: Every interactive/time-varying/viewport promise in the public brief maps to a criterion that tells the judge to act, wait or resize rather than score first paint. (1) Live updates ~5 s without reload, keeping half-typed reply, scroll and open thread (conversations.md:31): functional live_updates_keep_my_work (functional/judge.toml:221-230) opens a second browser context, scrolls the thread off the bottom, opens a reply box and types a draft, has Harriet post/reply/edit/delete, then checks 'without reloading, within about ten seconds' all four changes plus draft, open box and scroll position. (2) Wall takes effect live (walls-and-retention.md:19): wall_added_live (judge.toml:77-89) leg 1 'In Sian's page, without reloading, within about ten seconds M-13 disappears'. (3) Unread same in every tab (conversations.md:25): unread_and_new_messages_line (judge.toml:193-204) uses two Dev contexts and 'within about ten seconds, without reloading' counts in both, mark-unread moves the line. (4) Refusal reason stays until changed (walls-and-retention.md:37): polish refusal_in_place (polish/judge.toml:56-63) 'wait about ten seconds without touching anything' and rejects a passing toast. (5) Phone at ~390 px with no sideways scroll (conversations.md:33): polish phone_matter (polish/judge.toml:38-45) 'At 390 by 844 ... confirm documentElement.scrollWidth equals the viewport width and the message box is reachable'; visual prompt.md:49 'resize to 1440 by 900 first, and to 390 by 844 for the phone criterion', visual phone_chambers at 390x844. (6) Stale edit across two open pages: edits_and_stale_edit uses a second context with a still-open edit box. Hover-only marks are excluded (polish hold_mark 'visible without hovering'). Timer changes are checked as immediate effects ('disappears at once') against the fixed clock, so no real-time wait is needed. No theme or animation is requested in the brief, so none is graded. Global gates in functional/polish/visual prompts say 'a first-paint imitation does not pass'; app_context.md:24 gives the newContext recipe needed for the multi-context waits. Runtime: scripted golden harness (hash-verified, 2026-10-08 22:56-22:58Z) exercised these waits with real 10 s timeouts and measured #thread.scrollTop before/after (functional.cjs:85,198,457-475); golden-run.log lines show wall_added_live, unread_and_new_messages_line, live_updates_keep_my_work, polish_refusal_in_place PASS. Residual risk (why risk=true): no full configured LLM judge run exists, so it is unmeasured whether the judge actually waits/resizes as told; the phone/visual resize legs are not covered even by the scripted harness. Also Note: the 'within about ten seconds' windows are not given a single-action timing procedure (Colderwater lesson 7), so with LLM turn latency between Harriet's actions and the look at Gwen's/Sian's/Dev's page the effective window is likely longer than 10 s; a slow-polling app (e.g. 30 s, violating the brief's ~5 s) could pass live_updates_keep_my_work/wall_added_live. That is leniency in timing precision (rows 6/32 territory), not a failure to exercise the behaviour; the scroll leg also gives no explicit 'record scrollTop' step, leaving the judge to compare visually.
counterexample: Weak app that might pass: client polls every 30 s; because the judge spends several LLM turns performing Harriet's four writes before inspecting Gwen's page, elapsed time can exceed 30 s and the updates appear 'without reloading'. Conforming app that could fail: none found - a correct ~3-5 s poller/SSE app satisfies every 10 s window, the 720 px media query golden fits 390 px, and the phone legs only require scrollWidth==viewport and a reachable box. Neither is a defect of row 34 (judge is told to wait/resize/interact).
suggested_fix: Optional hardening (not required for this row): in the three 'within about ten seconds' criteria, tell the judge to perform the last remote write and the observing wait in one browser_run_code_unsafe action (e.g. waitForFunction with a 10 s timeout on the observer page) and to record #thread scroll position numerically before and after; then obtain a full configured judge run to measure that the waits/resizes are actually performed.
